commits.messageBody:
… (#1606)

New pipediff package: a structural diff that surfaces what actually
changed in a pipeline and hides the canvas coordinate churn that
dominates a raw JSON diff.

- engine.py: strict-JSON load + shape validation; match components by
  id; report added/removed nodes, provider changes, and a deep config
  diff rendered as dotted field paths (config.parameters.model:
  gpt-4 -> gpt-4o) over nested dicts and lists; reconstruct edges from
  each component's input[] (data lanes) AND control[] (agent
  orchestration wiring — present in most bundled examples) as a
  (from, lane, to) set diff.
- The ui block (position/measured), top-level viewport, and untouched-
  node layout are ignored by default and collapse to a single
  'layout changed' flag; include_layout surfaces them. A pure canvas
  move is never mistaken for a semantic change.
- gitref.py: resolve a pipe from a git ref via 'git show' (arg-list,
  never a shell string; None when the path is absent in the ref =
  all-added; PipeDiffError on git/parse failure).
- model.py: frozen FieldChange/EdgeChange + NodeChange/PipeDiff with a
  has_semantic_changes property.

49 unit tests (engine + gitref), including a real tmp-repo git
integration test.

commits.messageBody:
rocketride diff <old.pipe> <new.pipe>  |  --git <ref> <file.pipe>
[--include-layout] [--json] [--markdown] [--exit-zero]

Semantic pipeline diff for terminal and CI review. Unlike the other
subcommands it takes no connection args and never touches the engine or
network — it is pure local file/JSON/git work. Human output groups
Nodes/Edges/Config with +/-/~ markers (NO_COLOR and non-tty aware);
--json emits a single change document; --markdown emits PR-comment-safe
output (untrusted .pipe values are escaped so a config value can't break
out of a comment). Exit codes: 0 no semantic changes, 1 changes present,
2 usage/parse/git error; --exit-zero forces 0 for non-gating use.

30 tests (reporters + CLI) driving the full command against parsed
fixtures — no server required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

…ticky PR comment

On PRs touching .pipe files, renders each changed file's semantic diff
(vs the PR base) and posts/updates one sticky comment — turning 'review
pipelines like code' into visible review UX. Installs the rocketride CLI
(fails fast if the release lacks 'diff'; cli-version to pin), fetches the
PR base commit so it works with actions/checkout default fetch-depth 1,
and runs 'rocketride diff --git <base> <file> --markdown'. Third-party
actions pinned by commit SHA; GITHUB_TOKEN never echoed; needs
pull-requests: write (documented). No existing workflow files touched.

commits.messageBody:
…606)

Addresses the CodeRabbit review on #1607 and closes the gap between what
`--include-layout` documents and what it does.

- `--include-layout` now enumerates the top-level `viewport`. The flag's
  --help text and both docs pages promised "each node's ui block and the
  top-level viewport", but only per-node `ui` was ever diffed: a pan/zoom
  edit printed nothing and exited 0. `PipeDiff` gains `viewport_changes`
  (populated only under `include_layout`), it counts toward
  `has_semantic_changes`, and all three reporters render it — including a
  new `viewport` list and `summary.viewport_changes` count in the JSON
  document.
- `load_pipe()` and `_run_git()` map `UnicodeDecodeError` to
  `PipeDiffError`. It is a `ValueError`, not an `OSError`, so a non-UTF-8
  blob escaped the library API as a raw traceback.
- `_validate_pipe()` validates `input`/`control` wiring before edges are
  extracted. A non-list collection raised `TypeError`, an unhashable
  `from` blew up inside `set.add`, and a wire missing `from` silently
  produced a `(None, None, id)` edge. All three are now exit-2 errors
  naming the component and wire index.
- The Markdown renderer escapes the two values it still interpolated raw:
  the summary line's `version` and the caller-supplied `title`. Both go
  into an auto-posted PR comment, so a crafted value could break out into
  headings or @-mentions.
- The human renderer escapes CR/LF/ESC/C0 in ids, providers, lanes, paths
  and values via `_term_safe`, so a `.pipe` under review cannot rewrite
  the terminal it is being reviewed in.
- `pipediff/__init__.py` imports the reporters unconditionally; the
  try/except ImportError was scaffolding from the parallel implementation
  split and would have hidden a real packaging failure.
- `run()`'s docstring documents diff's 0/1/2 exit-code contract.
- The reporter tests use the production model classes instead of local
  mirrors that could drift from it.

22 new regression tests; 101 pass in the four pipediff files.

commits.messageBody:
…ing (#1606)

Addresses the CodeRabbit findings on the composite action, plus the
fork-PR gap they did not cover.

- The report is written to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on every exit path. The
  `comment: false` input already promised a job summary and nothing wrote
  one.
- The sticky-comment step tolerates a 403. On a `pull_request` event from
  a fork the default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only whatever the permissions
  block says, so commenting fails on exactly the PRs an open-source repo
  receives. It now warns and relies on the job summary instead of failing
  the check; the README documents the `comment: false` and
  `pull_request_target` trade-offs.
- New `install-from` input installs the CLI from a local path (e.g.
  `./packages/client-python`) instead of PyPI. Published `rocketride` is
  1.3.0 and has no `diff`, so until a release ships it the action could
  not be exercised at all.
- File names and CLI stderr are untrusted PR content and were
  interpolated raw into Markdown headings, a ``` fence, and `::error`
  annotations. Names now render through a double-backtick code span with
  newlines collapsed, error text uses a four-backtick fence, and the
  annotation message is stripped of newlines and `::`.
- Deleted `.pipe` files count as semantic (`has-semantic-changes: true`);
  a deletion-only PR previously reported "No semantic changes (layout
  only)". The exit-0 text no longer asserts "layout only" either — that
  is the CLI's own report to make.
- The sticky-comment lookup also checks the author is
  `github-actions[bot]`, so a human comment quoting the marker is not
  overwritten.
- The description and README scope the "no network" guarantee to the
  `rocketride diff` computation and name the traffic the action itself
  makes (pip install, git fetch, comments API).

Validated with PyYAML parse, `bash -n` on all four run blocks, `node
--check` on the github-script body, and an end-to-end run of the diff
step against a scratch repo (backticked filename, deletion, and unparsable
file paths all exercised).

…te ids (#1606)

Address the CodeRabbit review of the rebased head. Dispositions:

- action.yml L182-185/L312-316 (Markdown injection): FIXED. A path containing
  exactly two backticks closed the code span, and stderr containing a four-
  backtick fence line closed the error block, letting PR content escape into the
  auto-posted sticky comment. Both delimiters are now chosen per value by
  backtick_delim(), one backtick longer than the longest run in the untrusted
  string (min 2 for the span, 4 for the fence).
- action.yml L66-71 + action README (install-from as executable source): FIXED.
  Both now state that the value is handed to `pip install`, which executes the
  source's build/install code with the job's privileges and token, and that it
  must never resolve to PR-controlled code in a pull_request_target workflow.
- engine.py L147-150 (duplicate component ids): FIXED. _validate_pipe() tracks
  ids and raises PipeDiffError naming both indices; a duplicate previously
  shadowed the earlier node in _components_by_id() and hid it, and every change
  to it, from the diff. Regression test added.
- engine.py L290/L318 (layout normalization): FIXED. _layout_changed() now
  normalizes viewport/ui with `or {}` exactly as the layout field diffs do, so
  null-vs-{} no longer sets layout_changed with no ui.*/viewport.* change to
  show (which made --include-layout report a layout change and still exit 0).
  Parametrized regressions for null and omitted values on both.
- gitref.py L98 (unanchored stderr matching): FIXED. resolve_git_ref() verifies
  the ref with `rev-parse --verify --quiet <ref>^{commit}` and tests path
  presence with `cat-file -e`, both on exit codes. A ref whose *name* contained
  "does not exist in" was echoed back by git and matched the marker, silently
  turning a bad ref into an all-added diff instead of exit 2. Regression test
  added for that ref name.
- docs (pin actions to full SHAs): PARTIALLY FIXED. actions/checkout,
  actions/setup-python and marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment are pinned to
  reviewed commit SHAs with the usual `# vN` comment in all three documents,
  matching the convention in .github/workflows. pipe-diff@develop is left as a
  branch ref because the action is not yet released; the surrounding prose now
  explains why every `uses:` should be SHA-pinned.
- examples/pipe-diff-example.md L247-259 + cli.mdx (inline `pip install
  rocketride`): FIXED. `rocketride diff` ships in a release after 1.3.0, so the
  inline snippets installed a CLI without the subcommand. The in-repo example
  installs ./packages/client-python; the docs snippet carries the caveat and the
  working alternative.

commits.messageBody:
… install (#1606)

CodeRabbit round 2. Three independent defects, one per surface.

Workflow-command injection in the pipe-diff action. A workflow command is a
single line of the form "::error <prop>=<value>::<data>", so the PR-controlled
filename interpolated raw into file=${f} escaped the command: a name containing
a newline emitted forged ::warning:: lines of its own (verified: 3 command
lines before, 1 after), and a ":" or "," in it terminated the property list.
Percent-encode both the path and the CLI stderr exactly as @actions/core does
-- wc_escape_data covers %, CR and LF, wc_escape_property adds ":" and "," --
replacing the ad-hoc strip of newlines and "::" from the message. Encoding
rather than stripping also keeps the text intact, since GitHub renders %0A back
as a line break in the annotation.

Falsy layout values were normalized away in the engine. `... or {}` folded the
non-null falsy JSON values false, 0 and "" into {}, all of which load_pipe
accepts, so `viewport: false` versus `viewport: {}` produced no reported change
and exited 0 even under --include-layout. _layout_block normalizes only None,
in the layout flag and in both field diffs so the two still agree. Validation is
deliberately left alone: _validate_pipe rejects only shapes the diff cannot
process, and a scalar viewport/ui diffs fine through _diff_value's equality
fallback, so rejecting it would be stricter than the rest of the loader without
making any diff correct that is not already correct. Covered by parametrized
regression tests for false/0/"" on both viewport and node ui.

Docs installed a release that lacks `diff`. The inline workflow in cli.mdx ran
`pip install rocketride` under a comment explaining that no published release
provides the subcommand, so the very next step failed with
"invalid choice: 'diff'". Install the client package from a pinned commit of
this repository instead, and name both usable sources -- the in-repo path for
rocketride-server itself, the pinned git+https form for any other repository --
in cli.mdx and examples/pipe-diff-example.md so the two agree.

…606)

Python evaluates False == 0 and True == 1, so a viewport, ui, or config
value flipping between a boolean and a number produced no reported change
and --include-layout exited 0. _json_equal compares booleans only against
booleans and applies the rule recursively through dicts and lists; it now
backs both _layout_changed and _diff_value's scalar branch, so the layout
flag and the field diffs stay in lockstep.

Regressions: false<->0 / true->1 for viewport, node ui, and a config flag;
equal typed nested values still compare equal.

commits.messageBody:
The action documents — and the PR body claims — that the report reaches
`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on every path, which is what makes `comment: false`
and fork pull requests (read-only GITHUB_TOKEN -> 403 on the comments API)
usable at all. One path broke that promise: when the pull-request base
commit cannot be fetched, the step ran `echo "::error::…"; exit 1` before
`write_job_summary` was ever called, so the only trace of the failure was
a raw step log.

The failure now builds a marker-carrying body ("Could not fetch the
pull-request base commit `<sha>`" plus the actions/checkout remedy) and
calls `write_job_summary` before the annotation and `exit 1`, so the
summary explains the red check. The base SHA goes through `md_code` like
every other interpolated value. `write_job_summary` still no-ops when
`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is unset, so nothing regresses outside Actions.

The README's "Failure semantics" bullet now names both failure paths
(undiffable `.pipe` file, unfetchable base) and states that both write
the summary.

Validated with PyYAML `safe_load`, `bash -n` and `shellcheck -s bash` on
all four extracted `run:` blocks, `node --check` on the async-wrapped
github-script body, and the extracted-snippet end-to-end check of the
diff step against scratch repositories, extended from three scenarios to
five: base commit unfetchable -> exit 1 with a marker/reason/SHA in the
summary and the `::error` annotation still emitted; the same failure with
`GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` unset -> exit 1, clean stderr; plus the existing
semantic-change, no-`.pipe`-change, and unparsable-file-with-backticked-
path cases. 18/18 assertions pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

latestReviews.body:
The layout separation is drawn where it should be — per-node `ui` blocks and the top-level `viewport`, nothing wider — and `include_layout` enumerates them when they are wanted, so a pure-layout change is still reported as such rather than vanishing.

The composite action holds up: SHAs pinned, inputs passed through `env:` rather than interpolated into the shell, `set -euo pipefail`, and the `install-from` risk under `pull_request_target` documented in the input description itself.

This solves a problem we already have — the extension rewrites `.pipe` files on its own and buries real changes in layout churn.

Note it shares `cli.mdx`, `README-python-client.md` and the subcommand registry with the other three CLI PRs, so it will need a rebase depending on merge order.
